source: US Office of Personnel Management list of federal holidays: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-holidays/
valueLogic: The big four come at once. The Monday holidays follow. Juneteenth and Columbus Day are harder. Washington's Birthday is the tail and the best fact in the round - the holiday everyone calls Presidents' Day has never officially been renamed.
note: Presidents' Day is accepted for Washington's Birthday: not the legal name, but refusing it would bust almost everyone who knows the holiday. Indigenous Peoples' Day is a non-busting nudge toward Columbus Day rather than an alias, because it isn't the federal name and presidential proclamations have varied.

answers.name: Christmas Day
answers.fact: A federal holiday since 1870, in the first batch Congress ever designated.

answers.name: Thanksgiving
answers.fact: Fixed to the fourth Thursday in November by Congress in 1941.

answers.name: Independence Day
answers.fact: Also in the original 1870 batch, alongside Christmas and New Year's Day.

answers.name: New Year's Day
answers.fact: One of the four original federal holidays.

answers.name: Memorial Day
answers.fact: Moved to the last Monday in May by the Uniform Monday Holiday Act of 1968.

answers.name: Labor Day
answers.fact: The first Monday in September, made federal in 1894.

answers.name: Veterans Day
answers.fact: Originally Armistice Day, marking the end of the First World War in 1918.

answers.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Day
answers.fact: Signed into law in 1983 and first observed in 1986.

answers.name: Juneteenth
answers.fact: The newest, signed into law in 2021, marking emancipation reaching Texas in 1865.

answers.name: Columbus Day
answers.fact: The second Monday in October, and a federal holiday since 1937.

answers.name: Washington's Birthday
answers.fact: The legal federal name. Almost everyone calls it Presidents' Day, which is not official.

distractors.name: Easter
distractors.note: Not a federal holiday, and never has been.

distractors.name: Election Day
distractors.note: Not a federal holiday, despite repeated proposals.

distractors.name: Inauguration Day
distractors.note: A holiday for federal workers in the DC area only, not nationwide.

distractors.name: Indigenous Peoples' Day
distractors.note: The same Monday, and proclaimed alongside it in recent years, but the federal holiday's legal name is still Columbus Day.
